Use Tier 2: replace last-position-only supervision with dense causal next-item supervision while retaining the current SASRec architecture and sampled-softmax objective. Focus on data_processing_and_feature_engineering, model_design, and training_evaluation as parts of this single change. The latest trial achieved macro HR@10 of 0.39 versus the supplied baseline’s 0.505, with especially large losses on CDs_and_Vinyl and Movies_and_TV. A plausible cause is that each sampled prefix now supplies only one supervised position, substantially reducing the training signal compared with the original SASRec sequence loss.

Construct right-aligned training sequences with shifted positive targets at every nonpadding position, using only the existing training histories. Apply the existing 32-negative cross-entropy objective independently at those positions, exclude each user’s training interactions from negative sampling, and average valid-position losses within each user before averaging across the batch. Compute negative logits in position chunks to bound GPU memory, while keeping model dimensions, optimizer settings, training seed 42, and the epoch limit unchanged for a controlled experiment. This tests whether richer supervision improves shared item representations and transition learning without introducing another predictor.

Select exactly one checkpoint per category using validation HR@10 with 200 users, 99 unique negatives, and evaluation seed 42, then report the four-category macro average. Preserve the supplied splits and preprocessing seed 0, retain DATA_DIR = os.environ['GAGC_DATA_DIR'], and keep artifacts beneath the trial directory. Update the predictor writer alongside training so validation and host inference use identical history processing and the same trained model forward pass, loading exactly one checkpoint for each category.
